newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila resumes talks with rebels, extends truce.
newsitem.headline: Manila resumes talks with rebels, extends truce.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Tuesday the government had resumed stalled peace talks with communist rebels and had extended a unilateral ceasefire for another 30 days.

He said government negotiators were meeting with a panel of the leftist National Democratic Front (NDF) in the Netherlands, which is hosting the talks, and called it "a breakthrough" in efforts to end the 27-year insurgency.

Ramos told a news conference in central Ramblon town he had ordered the military to extend for another month a 60-day unilateral ceasefire that began in December. The news conference was broadcast on state radio.
"The breakthrough is they have resumed talking," he said.
The NDF, an umbrella organisation representing 13 dissident left-wing groups, suspended talks in November after Manila refused to release a captured union leader.
Ramos did not say what persuaded the NDF, which is fighting for a Marxist state, to return to the negotiating table. Many NDF leaders live in exile in the Netherlands.

He said the continued suspension of military hostilities would apply to other insurgent groups, including the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) with which Manila is holding separate talks. The MILF is fighting for an Islamic state in the southern islands.
The government concluded a peace deal in September last year with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), ending a 24-year, MNLF-led revolt for Moslem autonomy.
